title: Strategic microcommit bands and rolling buffer allocation for feature waves
creator: Ethan Morales
description: Problem: As we scale Redwood Dedicated and Private onboarding, individual initiatives spike runway demand mid-cycle causing repeated mid-cycle scope cuts and last-minute reassignments. This ticket defines a lightweight, operational mechanism: 'microcommit bands' (small reserved effort bands per initiative) plus a rolling buffer allocation that moves between initiatives based on objective signals. Objective: reduce emergency scope cuts, increase predictability of cross-team staffing, and preserve high-priority launches without over-committing engineering capacity. Scope: define band sizing heuristic, buffer governance, automation hooks for signal ingestion (usage, blocker count, deploy risk), rollout plan for next three cycles, and dashboards to track buffer depletion and rebalancing activity.
acceptance_criteria: A documented band-sizing algorithm (band = % of initiative FTEs or points) agreed by PMR and Eng leads
Automation prototype that reports buffer usage and recommends rebalances in the Console (prototype integration to staging Grafana dashboard)
Playbook for mid-cycle buffer borrow/lend with decision thresholds and required approvals documented in Confluence
Run two simulated rebalances in the next cycle runbook and present results to PM/Eng leadership
No more than one emergency all-hands scope cut for initiatives participating in pilot during the rollout quarter
decisions: Use dual-bucket approach: microcommit bands per initiative (short-term reserve) + centralized rolling buffer (cross-initiative reserve)
Band sizing default = max(10% of committed points, 1 FTE-week equivalent) with overrides by project lead and PM
Buffer replenishment triggered by predefined signals: >30% increase in production incidents, >40% variance in predicted vs actual velocity, or SLA regression flagged by telemetry
Approval flow: up to 25% of an initiative's band can be borrowed by on-call director auto-approved; >25% requires cross-functional PM+Eng sync and formal amendment in the cycle board
